You are doing a security audit of a Rust search engine called XERJ at /root/ab-run-p1/repo. Work statically.

Your assigned area: INGEST OF UNTRUSTED DOCUMENTS. Two parts:

Part A: the pipeline processors in /root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-wasm/src/ (3 files, ~2700 lines) and any ingest/processor code in /root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-api/src/es_compat.rs or xerj-engine that handles documents at index time. Hunt for:
- Panics on attacker-controlled document content (unwrap/index/substring slicing on multibyte UTF-8, arithmetic overflow in offsets)
- Processor configurations that let a document author execute something (script injection, template injection, path access)
- Resource blowups: a tiny document that triggers huge allocation/compute (e.g., regex on untrusted input, recursive structures, decompression)
- Any wasm execution of untrusted modules or wasm memory bugs

Part B: the autoindex client's hostile-file parsing in /root/ab-run-p1/repo/engine/crates/xerj-autoindex/src/ (~97k lines over 89 files). This crate crawls/reads files from a corpus provider and indexes them. Find the file-format parsers (archives: zip/tar/gz; documents: pdf/office; text detection; nested archive handling). Hunt for:
- Zip-slip / path traversal when extracting archives (writes outside target dir)
- Archive bombs (nested compression, symlink following)
- Unbounded memory from a small file (decompression without limits, size fields trusted)
- Panics reachable from a malformed file (unwrap on parse results, slice indexing with offsets read from the file)
- Symlink handling when walking directories

Method: list the files first (ls), find parsers via grep (zip, tar, gzip, deflate, extract, parse, sniff, magic bytes, mmap, symlink, walk). Read the parsers carefully. Verify each finding's reachability: who supplies the file? The threat model is "a malicious document/corpus provider" — so parsers of corpus files ARE in scope and attacker-controlled. Trace the call path from a file on disk to the vulnerable code.

Report back: concrete findings each with file path, line number (current on-disk line), short excerpt, why reachable, and a concrete malicious-input description. Rank by severity. Only verified findings. Return raw findings text.

[package]
name = "xerj-wasm"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true
description = "WASM pipeline crate for xerj — built-in transform plugins with optional WASM backend"

[dependencies]
xerj-common = { path = "../xerj-common" }
serde        = { workspace = true }
serde_json   = { workspace = true }
tracing      = { workspace = true }
thiserror    = { workspace = true }
anyhow       = { workspace = true }
bytes        = { workspace = true }
tokio        = { workspace = true }
chrono       = { workspace = true }
regex        = "1"

[dev-dependencies]
tokio    = { workspace = true, features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros"] }
tempfile = { workspace = true }
=== AUTOINDEX CARGO ===
[package]
name = "xerj-autoindex"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true
description = "xerj autoindex — point it at any folder and make the contents AI-searchable with zero configuration"

[dependencies]
# The machine-resource policy (cores, memory safe zone, thread priority) is
# shared with the server: one policy, one place (#240).
xerj-common = { path = "../xerj-common" }
anyhow.workspace = true
serde.workspace = true
serde_json.workspace = true
# Durable sync_begin replay needs exact decimal-to-f64 recovery without
# selecting serde_json's slower float parser for the whole server binary.
simd-json.workspace = true
chrono.workspace = true
regex = "1"
# Corpus recipes (`xerj corpus build`) are authored TOML: human-readable and
# commented, so licence reasoning sits next to the source it justifies and
# ships verbatim inside the pack as provenance.
toml.workspace = true
walkdir = "2"
# gitignore/.xerjignore matching (#276). ripgrep's matcher, used for its
# semantics only — traversal stays on walkdir so the existing symlink,
# hidden-file and unreadable-entry behaviour is unchanged.
# Licence: Unlicense OR MIT — compatible with XERJ's Apache-2.0.
ignore = "0.4"
encoding_rs = "0.8"
# `--watch`: cross-platform filesystem notifications (inotify on Linux,
# FSEvents on macOS, ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows), so live reindexing is
# one code path rather than three.
# Licence: CC0-1.0 — a public-domain dedication, no copyleft and no attribution
# condition, so redistributing it inside Apache-2.0 XERJ is unrestricted. Noted
# because CC0 carries no express patent grant, unlike Apache-2.0 itself; its
# transitive deps here are inotify (ISC), notify-types (CC0-1.0), mio (MIT),
# bitflags/log/libc (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Verified against each crate's own
# metadata, not against a summary.
# The debouncer is ours (`watch.rs`): notify-debouncer-full keeps a second file
# cache and its own rename bookkeeping, which is precisely the state this
# crate's journal already owns.
notify = "8.2"
xxhash-rust.workspace = true
memchr.workspace = true
rayon.workspace = true
libc = "0.2"
tempfile.workspace = true
fs2 = "0.4"
# ES-compat HTTP client. Blocking mode: all of autoindex is synchronous
# (std threads), invoked from the server binary via spawn_blocking.
reqwest = { workspace = true, features = ["blocking"] }
# SigV4 for the object-storage watcher (`objwatch::s3`): HMAC-SHA256 chain and
# the payload digest. Both are already in this workspace's lock file at these
# versions (xerj-cluster, xerj-fts, xerj-api), so this adds no new package —
# and it is far less than `aws-sdk-s3` would pull into a synchronous crate that
# needs exactly two S3 verbs. See objwatch/s3.rs for why not the SDK.
sha2 = "0.10"
hmac = "0.12"
# ed25519 detached signatures over pack SHA256SUMS (`harvest/sign.rs`).
# Already in the lock file via the TLS stack (rustls→ring 0.17), so this adds
# no new native build; here it is only a direct dependency of the corpus-pack
# publish/verify path.
ring.workspace = true


# --- AST code extraction (tree-sitter). Grammars expose a tree-sitter-language
# LanguageFn, decoupled from the core version, so one core serves all. ---
# Core 0.26: forced by tree-sitter-perl 1.1.2, the only #295 grammar with a
# hard (`links`) core dep — same story as the c-sharp 0.24→0.25 bump. Every
# other grammar binds through tree-sitter-language and does not care.
tree-sitter = { workspace = true }
tree-sitter-python = "0.23"
tree-sitter-c = "0.23"
tree-sitter-rust = "0.23"
tree-sitter-javascript = "0.23"
tree-sitter-go = "0.23"
tree-sitter-typescript = "0.23"
tree-sitter-java = "0.23"
tree-sitter-cpp = "0.23"
tree-sitter-ruby = "0.23"
tree-sitter-php = "0.23"
tree-sitter-c-sharp = "0.23"
tree-sitter-bash = "0.23"
# --- #295 Tier 1: mainstream languages users expect. Versions are the ones
# checked against crates.io in the issue; each must expose a Language loadable
# by core 0.26 (ABI 13–15) — the all-grammars smoke test enforces that.
# NOT `tree-sitter-kotlin` (0.3.8): that crate hard-links core >=0.21,<0.23
# and cannot coexist with core 0.26. The `-ng` fork is the maintained
# tree-sitter-language binding of the same fwcd grammar.
tree-sitter-kotlin-ng = "1.1"
tree-sitter-swift = "0.7"
tree-sitter-scala = "0.26"
tree-sitter-dart = "0.2"
tree-sitter-lua = "0.5"
tree-sitter-perl = "1.1"
tree-sitter-r = "1.3"
tree-sitter-julia = "0.23"
tree-sitter-haskell = "0.23"
tree-sitter-elixir = "0.3"
# --- #295 Tier 2: common in ecosystems we already serve.
# NOT tree-sitter-clojure: its only release (0.1.0) hard-links core ^0.25.6,
# mutually exclusive with the core 0.26 that Tier 1's perl grammar forces —
# revisit when a clojure release against 0.26 exists.
# NOT tree-sitter-sql: 0.0.2 is immature (the issue itself says evaluate
# first or defer) and `.sql` routing must not steal sqldump files — deferred.
tree-sitter-erlang = "0.20"
tree-sitter-ocaml = "0.25"
tree-sitter-zig = "1.1"
tree-sitter-objc = "3.0"
tree-sitter-groovy = "0.1"
tree-sitter-powershell = "0.26"
tree-sitter-fsharp = "0.3"
tree-sitter-nix = "0.3"
# --- #295 Tier 3: long tail, only where the grammar proves solid.
# NOT tree-sitter-nim / tree-sitter-crystal: their only releases (0.1.0) are
# toy grammars (~17 node types, no module/struct/def nodes — verified in
# their node-types.json); they cannot parse real code in either language and
# no alternative crate exists on crates.io.
tree-sitter-fortran = "0.6"
tree-sitter-matlab = "1.3"
tree-sitter-solidity = "1.2"
streaming-iterator = "0.1"


# Format-family extractors (new deps, isolated to this crate):
flate2 = "1"                                     # gzip streaming (rust backend)
pdf_oxide = { version = "=0.3.75", default-features = false, features = ["legacy-crypto"] }
csv = "1"                                        # streaming CSV with sniffed dialect
quick-xml = "0.41"                               # XML pull parser + DOCX internals
zip = { version = "2", default-features = false, features = ["deflate"] }  # DOCX container
serde_yaml = "0.9"                               # YAML multi-doc
# The one C dependency (bundled SQLite), isolated to this crate.
rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled"] }
mail-parser = "0.11.9"

# --- Object-storage source (#s3source). `aws-sdk-s3` was already a workspace
# dependency and unused; this is its first consumer. Apache-2.0.
#
# There is deliberately no `aws-config` here. Taking it would (a) bring the
# default `default-https-client` feature path back in through cargo's feature
# unification and with it aws-lc-rs — the C/asm crypto backend this workspace
# keeps out of the cross-compile matrix — and (b) give this crate a second,
# differently-configured S3 client with the SDK's own invisible retry layer.
# Credentials come from the environment and the client is built explicitly in
# `src/objsource.rs`, the same way `xerj-storage` builds its own; the feature
# selection that keeps aws-lc-rs out is pinned in engine/Cargo.toml.
aws-sdk-s3 = { workspace = true }
aws-smithy-http-client = { workspace = true }
# autoindex is synchronous (std threads + rayon); the AWS SDK is async-only, so
# one current-thread runtime is created per object-store source and every call

## SYSTEMIC ROOT CAUSE

One design gap accounts for B4, B5, B7, B8 and amplifies B1: **streaming extractor families receive no cap on gzip-decompressed bytes, and several receive no per-record field-count cap.** `open_reader` (`extract/mod.rs:114-128`) applies `take(n)` only when the caller passes `Some(limit)`, and phase B passes `None` (`lib.rs:7291`). Meanwhile the size gate at `lib.rs:2341-2356` covers only `Json | Html | Yaml | TxtProse | Pdf | Docx` — exempting `Csv, Logs, SqlDump, Jsonl, Mbox, UnityYaml, Eml, Sqlite`. Adding a decoded-byte `take` in `open_reader` for full runs, a record-size limit in csv/sqldump, and `MAX_FIELDS_PER_RECORD` in csv/logs/sqldump closes the entire class.
